channels.name: Identity, Auth & Access Control
channels.evidence: WAVE 8 RE-JUDGED THIS DOWNWARD. A fresh critic with a mutation-test budget scored this piece 4/10 where my board had the channel at 7. The repair round then addressed the named gap, but NOTHING HAS RE-JUDGED THE REPAIR — so this number reflects what a critic actually measured, not what a builder reported afterwards. THE WORST VERDICT OF THE WAVE, and it is the security channel. The critic's words: the identity model is untouched, and the two things it is claimed to protect both fall over. Six fabrications in one lane. Authentication is still three shared passwords that double as their own session tokens — no users, no real logout, and rate limiting that the critic did not find convincing. I am taking this down two points rather than one because a channel that guards access should never be scored on intent, and because everything I previously credited it with came from a builder's own account rather than an adversarial one. WHAT WOULD MOVE IT: real sessions replacing the shared passwords, and every refusal proven BOTH WAYS — the denied case getting a real status, the allowed case still succeeding.
channels.goal_text: builderz-labs — per-agent API keys and viewer/operator/admin roles over real sessions, replacing three shared passwords that double as their own tokens.

channels.name: Work Management API (MC API)
channels.evidence: The code-review lifecycle completes AND the bug lifecycle is unblocked. `environment` was required by a validator and was not a column, so a bug moving defined->open answered 400 without it and 500 with it — every bug in this installation was stuck, in both directions, and the Bug Details panel read "No bug details provided" on every bug ever opened. Now 200 with the fields stored. A body carrying the phantom column returns 422 NAMING the real columns rather than 500, which matters because lib/agent-queue.ts still instructs the Tester agent to send it — the outage was one agent run from returning. The MC API also no longer routes work to agents that do not exist. Held back: limit=0 still means every matching row and two callers use it to read one integer, and the API still returns raw CHECK constraint text for an invalid enum value.
channels.goal_text: Linear's issue list — server-side paging with an exact total, so no screen ever shows a number computed from a truncated slice.

channels.name: Portability & Host Independence
channels.evidence: npm install really was broken, on the owner's own primary goal, at step one. This host genuinely has no C++ toolchain, so a fresh copy failed the way a new user's would: gyp ERR! find VS. Not simulated. The builder traced the cause into npm's arborist source rather than guessing — the synthetic node-gyp rebuild step gates on pkg.gypfile !== false, and lockfileVersion 3 has no slot for gypfile, so resolving from the lockfile always reads undefined there whatever better-sqlite3's own manifest says. With the field added: install exit 0, npm ci exit 0, prebuilt binary used, no build directory. The better half is the durability gap it then found — a plain npm install silently strips that field back out on its next write — so there is a test, and I proved it myself by removing the field and watching it fail BY NAME, then restoring. A full clone-to-running trial was run TWICE from fresh copies: install, setup, doctor, dev, /api/health, login, an unauthenticated 401, then an authenticated create and read. HELD BACK: macOS and Linux are unverified, npm run build and npm start were not exercised (build is forbidden on this host), and a genuinely reachable Postgres was never tested — only the dead-endpoint path.
channels.goal_text: builderz-labs — SQLite and one start command, no Redis, Postgres or Docker. Clone it, run it, working app on any OS with no cloud account.

channels.name: LLM Provider Independence
channels.evidence: This channel carried a FALSE evidence string for several waves: "66 remaining references — chat still routes to a cloud host the owner has ruled out". A builder measured it and both halves are wrong. Live code across app/lib/components/hooks contains ZERO references to the ruled-out provider, comments stripped or not. Chat routes to LLM_BASE_URL, which is http://localhost:11434/v1 — proven live rather than read: a cloud model id returns 400 naming the local endpoint it is not present in, and a local qwen2.5-coder id returns 200 with an SSE stream. The model list is proxied from that endpoint, so it is live rather than hardcoded, and a new test locks the dangerous shape — an unreachable or empty roster must error naming the URL and must NOT fall back to a constant. The provider is genuinely a base URL: selection is an env var, resolveProvider refuses to default to a cloud host, and tiers resolve against the live roster rather than a static map. A new guard derives its banned set from the "Never X" bullets in HANDOFF.md rather than carrying its own list. Held back: two migration CHECK constraints still ADMIT a ruled-out connection type on a legacy table with no callers, and two CLI runtimes map tiers to hardcoded vendor ids because their provider is a binary, not a base URL — there is no seam to move them onto.
channels.goal_text: LiteLLM — the provider is a base URL, not a code branch. Open WebUI — the model list is read live from that endpoint, never hardcoded.

channels.name: Data Layer & Schema Management
channels.evidence: Migration 066 restores four columns that a live validator required and the schema did not have — environment, steps_to_reproduce, expected_behavior, actual_behavior — and DELIBERATELY does not add test_status, with both halves of that reasoning in the migration comment. The evidence for the split was measured, not argued: across 3,078 production rows in the Supabase export the stored test_status disagreed with the derived value on 372 of them, 12.1 percent, with passed sitting on rows whose tester and designer were both still pending. A stored duplicate of a derived value that was already wrong one time in eight. A new no-phantom-columns guard compares every column named in live code against the LIVE schema and is proven in both directions across writes, filters, selects and query strings — and states in its own header the case it would NOT catch, which is the interface declaration where this defect lived longest. WAVE 6 KEPT THIS AT 8 RATHER THAN RAISING IT, because a dialect asymmetry sat in the seam the whole time: an equality filter on a schema-declared BOOLEAN column bound a string, which Postgres infers correctly for free and SQLite never matches. Every Postgres-run test passed. The seam's two-dialect discipline is exactly what this channel scores, and it had a hole only the host a fresh clone actually runs could see. WAVE 7 closed the gap the previous fix could not reach and added a ninth guard for the class. Three columns are declared boolean in postgres and plain INTEGER in their sqlite twins, so the type-keyed hook was blind to them; no filter targets them today, so what existed was a trap whose trigger was 'somebody writes an ordinary filter'. The builder chose a curated override map over rebuilding two hot-path tables that every live agent-runtime wrapper writes to continuously, and deliberately did NOT leave a migration file on disk where an unattended db:migrate could pick it up before a maintenance window exists. I proved the new guard both ways myself, and — because this repo has twice shipped a guard that ran nowhere — confirmed the smoke test exits 1 with a gap planted and 0 without. Also measured this wave: the eq coercion works INSIDE an or(...) clause, which a critic had flagged as possibly a separate parse path.
channels.goal_text: builderz-labs — migrations run at first DB access, so starting the app creates the schema. No migrate command to know about, no colliding prefixes.

channels.name: Observability & Honest Reporting
channels.evidence: WAVE 8 closed the held-back item and found its twin still live. lib/llm-provider.ts had silently defaulted a JSON-parse failure to an empty model list, so a server that is not OpenAI-compatible reported the IDENTICAL 'reachable, 0 models' a real Ollama with nothing pulled reports — two very different problems, one indistinguishable answer, and the one an operator would act on was the invisible one. Fixed. This was the only lane of ten whose critic said it MEETS its goal, at 8/10. It still does not go up, because that same critic found the identical defect STILL LIVE ONE FILE OVER at lib/runtimes/openai-api.ts:136 — fixed in the same file, missed in its neighbour, which is how a whole class survives a fix that was genuinely correct.
channels.goal_text: Paperclip — full tool-call tracing and an audit log per ticket. LangSmith — drill from a cost number to the run and step that caused it.

channels.name: Work Management UI
channels.evidence: WAVE 8 RE-JUDGED THIS DOWNWARD. A fresh critic with a mutation-test budget scored this piece 5/10 where my board had the channel at 7. channels.name: Agent Fleet Operations
channels.evidence: WAVE 8 RE-JUDGED THIS DOWNWARD. A fresh critic with a mutation-test budget scored this piece 6/10 where my board had the channel at 7. The repair round then addressed the named gap, but NOTHING HAS RE-JUDGED THE REPAIR — so this number reflects what a critic actually measured, not what a builder reported afterwards. THE REAL WIN HERE IS NOT THE SCORE. Three of the five 'known failures' that had been red for the ENTIRE program — agents-route and agents-unconfigured — are fixed. Every gate report I have written said '5 known failures' and moved past them, including my own, for eight waves. A permanently red test is a test nobody reads, and it took a standing instruction to find out why rather than to route around it. Only spawn-live remains, and it is a genuine environment dependency. channels.name: Run Safety & Enforcement
channels.evidence: A second layer of protection had been silently off and nothing said so. An equality filter on the blocked flag matched ZERO rows on the live SQLite host — no error, an empty result indistinguishable from 'there are none' — and that filter is ANDed into the eligible-issues query for EIGHT OF NINE agent-queue lanes, is main's entire blocked-issue triage filter, and sits in four WIP-ceiling counts. A ceiling whose count always reads 0 never fires. It hid because the is-filter parses to a real boolean while the eq-filter stays a string, so the two read as synonyms; and because Postgres infers the parameter type for free, so every Postgres-run test passed while SQLite — what a fresh clone runs — compared TEXT to INTEGER and never matched. Fixed at the seam rather than the call sites, on the SQLite flavour only, keyed off the schema-declared column type so a text column genuinely holding the word 'false' is untouched; proven red-then-green on both dialects and over real HTTP. The dispatch kill switch was never affected and both of its acceptance checks still pass. HELD BACK, and stated rather than fixed: three more boolean-meaning columns are declared INTEGER rather than BOOLEAN in the sqlite migrations, so they would reproduce this exactly the moment a query-string filter targeted one, and this fix cannot catch them because it keys off the declared type. Also the ceilings have never been observed FIRING against a real dispatch run, because dispatch is off by owner directive.
channels.goal_text: Paperclip — budgets per agent, and at the limit they stop. Portkey — the cap is enforced in the request path, outside the agent, so it cannot be reasoned past.

channels.name: Learning & Memory Loop
channels.evidence: The chain was already built — my briefing said 'nothing populates the store' and that was WRONG, the ninth wrong briefing this session; all four runtime adapters already called the exit hook and 37 tests were green. What was true is that the table held zero rows, so it had never been EXERCISED. A critic reproduced it end to end with its own vocabulary: real API transitions setting rejection_count by the app's own rule, a real spawn, a real row written on process exit, then retrieval on a task key that never existed, matching on FTS5 vocabulary alone. It also built a PGlite harness nobody had run and proved the Postgres keyword-overlap fallback is REAL, not a stub, with an explicit incomplete-scan flag so a bounded scan cannot masquerade as a complete search — it scored that as BEATING the competitor, which is SQLite-only. THE GAP IT FOUND: the exit hook never selected the issue title, so every lifecycle row carried a null title — and both engines index that field. A run finishing CLEANLY, with no rejection, wrote a row whose only searchable content was a task key the ranker deliberately strips: an unsearchable record. Fixed and pinned by a test that retrieves a clean run by title alone. A budget overflow now surfaces as 503 with its token numbers instead of an unstructured 500, with the claim reverted so an issue does not sit claimed with nothing running. HELD BACK: what was attempted, whether it succeeded, and the exit status are still null on every lifecycle row — deferred deliberately, since no real exit code is available at that call site — so a record says what was rejected, not what was tried. And the loop never closes automatically here because dispatch is off by owner directive.
channels.goal_text: Hermes Agent — records what it tried and failed after each task, retrieves it on similar ones by FTS5, and caps in-context memory so overflow errors instead of truncating.

channels.name: Navigation & Deep Linking
channels.evidence: WAVE 8: a RUN now has a URL that survives a reload, which was the exact clause holding this below goal — the goal text names 'LangSmith: every trace has a URL' and an individual run had no address at all. Before the fix, buildPath emitted [p, <slug>, 'runs'] and erased the /r/<id> milliseconds after load, so a run URL worked on a click and never on a reload. The lane could not apply the seam itself, so it SHIPPED A TEST SUITE THAT WAS RED ON PURPOSE and whose failure message printed the entire diff — incompleteness moved out of prose and into the gate, where it cannot be forgotten. I applied it; all four pass. HELD AT 7 rather than raised, because the same critic found a leak test that COULD NOT FAIL: it widened the selected columns to include the agent transcript and the server log path, the suite reported 50 passed / 50 total, and the live endpoint then returned both at HTTP 200. The repair killed that mutant and five others that had survived the previous round, including an anchor test that passed when the anchor was a span. None of that has been re-judged.
channels.goal_text: Slack — every message has a permalink that opens it in context. LangSmith — every trace has a URL. Linear — any view is a link. No screen unreachable.

channels.name: Approval & Human-in-the-loop
channels.evidence: WAVE 8 RE-JUDGED THIS DOWNWARD. A fresh critic with a mutation-test budget scored this piece 5/10 where my board had the channel at 7. channels.name: Pipeline Fidelity
channels.evidence: WAVE 8 RE-JUDGED THIS DOWNWARD. A fresh critic with a mutation-test budget scored this piece 6/10 where my board had the channel at 7. The repair round then addressed the named gap, but NOTHING HAS RE-JUDGED THE REPAIR — so this number reflects what a critic actually measured, not what a builder reported afterwards. SEVEN FABRICATIONS, the most of any lane, and the headline one is structural: the humaniser is a whitelist masquerading as a rule, and none of its guards can tell. So raw database text can still reach the operator through any refusal nobody happened to think of — and the whole point of this channel is that it never does. A whitelist is only as good as the imagination of whoever wrote it, and it reports full coverage either way.
channels.goal_text: Linear — group a board by any dimension, every column a real status. Plane — swim lanes. Todero adds a lane per agent, so you see what each one is working through.

channels.name: Customer Conversations
channels.evidence: The transport SEAM exists; the transport does not, and that is deliberate — the provider is an open decision on this board and no agent was allowed to pick one. What landed: a provider-agnostic inbound webhook with its OWN dedicated credential, idempotency (a real provider retries, and a repeat delivery now answers 200 duplicate with the original row instead of creating a second customer message), an outbound adapter interface with ZERO implementations that refuses an unapproved draft both at runtime and by type, and reply-level threading inside a conversation — migration 070, both dialects. The builder re-measured all four 'already good' claims instead of assuming them, including re-running the approve-gate CHECK constraint in both dialects and the draft-cannot-approve-its-own 201-then-403 against the live server. It also found a structural limit and refused to work around it: middleware gated every /api/* route on a session or the GENERAL internal secret before any handler ran, so its dedicated credential was correct and still unreachable without also knowing Todero's general secret. It wrote the diff and left the shared file alone. I applied it only after measuring all three refusals myself — no auth 401 from middleware, wrong secret 401 from the route saying 'refused, not passed through to any other check', and an UNCONFIGURED secret still refusing rather than becoming a bypass. Card verified in a browser: 'Who is waiting on a reply? / 0 awaiting approval' with the query printed. HELD BACK: no provider, so an outbox that cannot send is still a draft folder; and the VALID webhook path is proven at the route level only — the env var is unset here and restarting the server is forbidden.
channels.goal_text: Slack — a reply threads instead of drowning the channel. Grok Bot — drafts while you are away, surfaces only what needs approval. You approve; Todero sends.

channels.name: Multi-tenancy & Identity
channels.evidence: EXEMPT BY OWNER DECISION, 2026-08-26. Two standing orders contradicted: 'the loop ends when every channel clears its goal' and 'multi-tenancy is post-MVP, skip it'. This channel sits at 1/8 and was being skipped every wave while the completion condition counted it — so the loop was running toward a finish line it had already been told to make unreachable. Done is now 18 of 18 SCORED channels. This one is still shown, with its real number, because an exemption you can see is honest and a deleted row is not. IF THIS EVER CHANGES: Todero hosting a second customer's business alongside Limiglow is the trigger, and it is the one channel whose absence is invisible until the day it is catastrophic — schema, scoping, and every guard.
channels.goal_text: Linear — sign in and see only your workspace. Anyone runs Todero for their own business and projects, isolated from everyone else.

channels.name: Secrets & Credential Custody
channels.evidence: Custody stopped being decorative. The operator could add a Discord credential to a hub and see it stored, and exactly ONE of the app's send paths consulted it — every other notification came from a process-wide env var. Counting it took three tries: a builder reported seven direct env reads, I corrected it to eight after grepping myself, and the next builder found NINE across seven files, because status/route.ts has two and everyone had counted it as one. All nine now resolve through lib/discord-sender.ts, which wraps resolveHubDiscord, keeps the env var as a documented fallback, and refuses BY NAME when neither exists. One site had been doing console.error('message dropped') — a silent drop from the operator's side, since nobody watching the app ever learned it had not gone. Two sites deliberately do NOT thread a hub id because none is in scope there, and the code says so rather than implying resolution it does not do. I read the app/api/issues/route.ts diff line by line myself — it has broken production twice this session — and it touches postDiscord and notifyWatchers and nothing else; grepping it for isOwnerActor, KAOS_ROLES, scope, transition, validator, permission, backlog and archived returns one hit, the word 'scoped' inside a new comment. HELD BACK HARD: the OpenRouter key is still live in origin/main's history until the owner rotates it. And only ENV custody was exercised live — stored/encrypted custody could not be, since the encryption key is unset in this process.
channels.goal_text: Doppler / Vercel env — secrets encrypted at rest, scoped per service, revocable without redeploy, and never printed. Todero holds delegated tokens only.

channels.name: Search & Findability
channels.evidence: CLEARED. Enter opens the issue itself rather than landing on a destination default, results open in context over the surface that would otherwise list them, and the modifiers narrow to the one you meant. A critic scored in: as BEATING Slack — it validates against all 16 real statuses, names them all on failure, and fires ZERO network requests on a bad value, where Slack simply returns nothing. before: had been a shape regex that accepted 9999-99-99 and 2026-13-45, issued a live query and rendered results under 'issues matching this filter'; calendar-impossible dates are refused now. from: was case-sensitive and unvalidated, so a capitalised name returned 'no issue matches', indistinguishable from 'that person has no issues'. And the filters now live in the URL via replaceState, which was the remaining half of Linear's 'any view is a link' — they had been held in the palette's local state and lost on close. Every verb the palette offers was executed against the live API: 9 offered all PATCH 200, all 6 withheld ones genuinely refuse, and withheld moves now show their real reason instead of vanishing. WHAT KEEPS IT AT 8 RATHER THAN HIGHER: from: is case-insensitive but still not validated against the real assignee roster, so a name that does not exist reads as a person with no work — Slack will not let you type a non-existent user without seeing it. That is the one place this still loses.
channels.goal_text: Slack search — modifiers like in:, from:, before: that narrow 2,440 records to the one you meant, and results that open in context rather than a dead list.
